chains.title: GABPA alt-gaining ETS site activates TERT
chains.element: The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal, consistent with an active TERT upstream promoter element, although the cCRE z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples rather than glioblastoma-specific.
chains.cell_type: Glioblastoma, with relevance to melanoma and bladder cancer

links.claim: GABPA binds the alt allele more strongly. The GABPA own QBiC-SELEX model gives alt effect +4.05 (z 71.32; E32), and the shared Ets model also gives alt-gaining binding (E17). GABPA ENCODE peaks contain the variant in HepG2 and SK-N-SH (E33), but E04 states that no ENCODE biosample matches the glioblastoma expression context, so disease-context occupancy is not established. I choose GABPA over ETV2/ETV3/FLI1 because GABPA has an own QBiC model and some ChIP occupancy, whereas those rely on an ETV5-mapped model and have unknown occupancy.
The variant is in a promoter-like cCRE with active chromatin marks, so an allele-specific TF change could alter promoter activity.
TERT is the nearest coding gene at 0.0 kb and the variant is annotated as a TERT upstream promoter variant, making TERT the target gene.

Glioblastoma is a relevant context because GABPA is expressed at 15.52 TPM in DepMap glioblastoma lines and TERT promoter mutations are reported in glioblastoma; this supports disease context, not GABPA occupancy in that context.

Predicted phenotype: alt-enhanced GABPA binding increases TERT promoter activity and telomerase, supporting tumor maintenance. General TERT promoter mutation literature supports novel TF-site/TERT activation (E34d), but a pooled screen reported no detected ETS-factor dependency for TPMs (E34b), so the phenotype is a model prediction rather than demonstrated.

predictions: Alt allele shows stronger GABPA ChIP/CUT&RUN signal at this base in a relevant cell type.
Alt allele increases TERT reporter activity in glioblastoma cells in a GABPA-dependent manner.
GABPA knockdown reduces the alt-dependent TERT increase.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA occupancy or a ref/alt TERT reporter assay in glioblastoma cells fails to show alt-enhanced GABPA binding or GABPA-dependent TERT activation.
The alt allele does not increase TERT expression or telomerase activity in a relevant cell type.
GABPA is not expressed or not bound at this element in the disease-relevant cell type.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of this base
predictions: No allele-specific TF occupancy at this exact base in disease-relevant cells.
Disease association is explained by a linked causal variant, recurrent somatic mutational hotspot/passenger status, or no allelic TF effect.
TERT activation, if present, is not mediated by a TF binding change at this base.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TF occupancy and reporter assays in relevant cells show that this base directly changes TF binding and TERT expression.
A linked causal variant is excluded and the C250T base itself is shown to be functional.

chains.title: ETV3 alt-gaining Ets site activates TERT, weak because the model is shared and occupancy is unknown
chains.element: The variant lies in the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530.

links.claim: ETV3 binds the alt allele more strongly in the shared ETV5-mapped Ets QBiC-SELEX model (effect +2.421, z 167.5; E28). ETV3 occupancy at this site is unknown because ENCODE never assayed ETV3, and the model is not ETV3-specific, so this binding evidence is weak.
The variant is in an active promoter-like cCRE, so an ETV3 site change could affect promoter output.
TERT is the nearest gene and the variant is annotated as a TERT upstream promoter variant.
Glioblastoma is a plausible context because ETV3 is expressed at 8.69 TPM in DepMap glioblastoma lines and TERT promoter mutations occur in glioblastoma.

Predicted phenotype: alt-enhanced ETV3 binding would increase TERT transcription and telomerase activity. No direct ETV3-C250T perturbation evidence is cited, and the shared ETV5-mapped model makes this a weak prediction.

predictions: ETV3 ChIP or allele-specific binding assay shows alt-enhanced occupancy at this base in glioblastoma cells.
ETV3 depletion reduces alt-dependent TERT expression.
ETV3 binding correlates with TERT expression in relevant tumor cells.
falsified_if: ETV3 is not expressed or not bound at the TERT promoter in glioblastoma cells.
Allele-specific assays show no ETV3 occupancy difference at this base.
Alt-dependent TERT activation remains after ETV3 depletion.

chains.title: Loss of KLF12 repressor on the alt allele derepresses TERT, speculative
chains.element: The variant lies in the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530.
chains.cell_type: Glioblastoma, but KLF12 relevance is weak because expression is low

links.claim: KLF12 binds the ref allele more strongly in QBiC-SELEX (effect -0.439, z -15.38; E18). The best model is KLF5-mapped and KLF12 ChIP is only in HepG2, so factor-specific disease-relevant occupancy is weak.
The variant is in an active promoter-like cCRE, so loss of a repressive TF site could change promoter activity.
TERT is the nearest gene and is annotated as the upstream promoter target.
KLF12 relevance to glioblastoma is weak: it is expressed at only 4.47 TPM in DepMap glioblastoma lines, and no disease-context occupancy is shown.
Speculative phenotype: if KLF12 represses TERT, then the alt allele losing KLF12 binding would derepress TERT and increase telomerase activity. No direct evidence shows KLF12 represses TERT.

predictions: KLF12 ChIP signal is stronger on the ref allele at this base.
The alt allele shows reduced KLF12 occupancy and increased TERT reporter activity.
falsified_if: KLF12 is not expressed or not bound at the TERT promoter in glioblastoma cells.
Alt allele does not reduce KLF12 occupancy at this base.
KLF12 loss does not derepress TERT in relevant cells.

grades_v0.reason: E17 gives a strong alt-gaining QBiC-SELEX change for GABPA (z 167.5, effect +2.421), but the cited occupancy is ENCODE ChIP in HepG2/SK-N-SH only; E04 explicitly says no ENCODE biosample matches the glioblastoma expression context, so no peak counts as bound here. The best QBiC model is also ETV5-mapped, not GABPA-specific.

E03 directly places the variant in PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal, consistent with an active promoter-like element. Caveat: the z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
E01 annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant; E02 places TERT 0.0 kb from its TSS and as the nearest coding gene.

E17 shows GABPA is expressed at 15.52 TPM in DepMap glioblastoma, and E15 includes TERT promoter-mutant glioblastoma literature. This supports disease context, though not GABPA occupancy in that context.

E15 is only a broad Europe PMC result list with titles, not evidence that alt-enhanced GABPA binding at C250T increases TERT expression, telomerase activity, or tumor maintenance. The mechanistic phenotype is asserted, not shown.

E28 is QBiC-SELEX only (alt effect +2.421, z 167.5); ETV3 occupancy is unknown because ENCODE never assayed it. The shared ETV5-mapped model and absence of relevant occupancy make this weak, not supported.
E03 places the variant in the active PLS cCRE EH38E3622530. Same caveat: activity marks are maxima over biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
E01 and E02 support TERT as the nearest gene and the variant as a TERT upstream promoter variant.
E28 shows ETV3 is expressed at 8.69 TPM in DepMap glioblastoma, and E15 supports TERT promoter mutations in glioblastoma. This is expression/context support, not functional evidence.
No cited evidence links ETV3 binding at this base to TERT transcription or telomerase activity; E15 is generic TERT/disease literature.

E18 gives a ref-gaining QBiC-SELEX change (effect -0.439, z -15.38), but KLF12 ChIP is only in HepG2 ('bound elsewhere'), not glioblastoma; E04 says no matching biosample peak counts as bound. The best model is KLF5-mapped, and KLF12 expression is low at 4.47 TPM.
E03 places the variant in the active PLS cCRE EH38E3622530, so the element context is supported, with the same biosample-max caveat.
E01 and E02 support TERT as the nearest gene and upstream promoter target.

KLF12 is expressed in DepMap glioblastoma but only at 4.47 TPM (rank 787); E15 supports TERT promoter mutations in glioblastoma but does not show KLF12 is functional or relevant in that context. Low expression weakens the relevance claim.
The claim requires KLF12 to be a TERT repressor and loss of its site to derepress TERT, but no cited assay supports KLF12 repression at TERT; E15 is generic disease literature.

grades_final.reason: QBiC-SELEX supports alt-gaining GABPA binding (own model effect +4.05, z 71.32; E32/E17), and GABPA ChIP peaks contain the variant in HepG2/SK-N-SH (E33). However E04 states no ENCODE biosample matches the glioblastoma expression context, so relevant-cell-type occupancy is not established. One side (binding change) is present, but occupancy is not in the disease-relevant cell type, making the link weak rather than supported.

E03 directly places the variant in cCRE EH38E3622530, a promoter-like (PLS) element with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal. The claim appropriately notes these are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.

E01 annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant in a TERT promoter regulatory feature, and E02 places TERT at 0.0 kb from its TSS. This directly supports TERT as the nearest/annotated target gene.

E17 shows GABPA expression in DepMap glioblastoma lines (15.52 TPM, rank 303/1626), and E15 provides glioblastoma TERT-promoter literature context. The claim limits itself to disease context and does not assert glioblastoma GABPA occupancy.

General TERT promoter mutation literature supports TERT activation via novel TF sites (E34d), but there is no direct GABPA/C250T perturbation or reporter evidence. E34b additionally reports no detected ETS-factor dependency in a pooled TPM screen. The phenotype remains an indirect model prediction.

E28 gives an alt-gaining QBiC-SELEX change for an ETV5-mapped model (effect +2.421, z 167.5), but the model is not ETV3-specific and ETV3 occupancy is unknown because ENCODE never assayed ETV3. QBiC-SELEX alone is at best weak support for a binding link.
E03 directly supports that the variant lies in an active promoter-like cCRE (EH38E3622530).
E01 and E02 directly annotate the variant as a TERT upstream promoter variant and place TERT at 0.0 kb from the TSS.
E28 shows ETV3 expression in DepMap glioblastoma lines (8.69 TPM), and E15 supplies glioblastoma TERT-promoter context. This supports a plausible disease context, not occupancy.

The phenotype is an indirect prediction from general TERT promoter mutation mechanisms (E34d, E15). There is no ETV3-specific perturbation or allele-specific reporter evidence, and the shared ETV5-mapped model further weakens the specific ETV3 claim.

E18 supports ref-gaining KLF12 binding in QBiC-SELEX (effect -0.439, z -15.38), but the best model is KLF5-mapped and KLF12 ChIP is only in HepG2. Factor-specific disease-relevant occupancy is not established.
E03 directly places the variant in the promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 with active chromatin marks.
E01 and E02 directly support TERT as the nearest/annotated upstream promoter target.
E18 shows only low KLF12 expression in DepMap glioblastoma lines (4.47 TPM, rank 787/1626) and no glioblastoma-context occupancy. The claim itself admits weak KLF12 relevance.
No evidence is cited to show that KLF12 represses TERT or that loss of KLF12 binding at the alt allele derepresses TERT. The phenotype is speculative and lacks direct support.

Tests directly whether ENCODE has GABPA occupancy over this variant in the disease-relevant context; absence would keep the binding link weak or missing.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr5:1295135:G>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap subtype median Glioblastoma), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 18 occupied (14 with a strong site), 5 of 145 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 0 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 554 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 1 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.

Here we used pooled CRISPR/Cas9-based approaches to identify vulnerabilities associated with telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations (TPMs) found in >80% of glioblastomas.
However, we could not detect dependencies on either TERT itself or on an E-twenty six transcription (ETS) factor known to activate TPMs.

Point mutations in the core promoter region of the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) gene have been found to occur at high frequencies in several tumour types and considered a primary cause of telomerase reactivation in cancer cells.

These mutations promote TERT gene expression by multiple mechanisms, including the generation of novel binding sites for nuclear transcription factors, displacement of negative regulators from DNA G-quadruplexes, recruitment of epigenetic activators and disruption of long-range interactions between TERT locus and telomeres.

A growing number of recent studies suggest that the most common mutations in the TERT promoter (ATG start site -124C>T and -146C>T) are associated with increased TERT mRNA expression, telomerase activity, telomere length, and poor prognosis.
